title: Pre-Purchase Inspection Hamburg | Container Ships & Feeders
description: Pre-purchase ship inspection in Hamburg for buyers of container ships, feeders and bulk carriers: deck, holds, tanks and machinery checked on the Elbe.
h1: Buying a container ship sold from Hamburg: inspection at the terminal, the mooring dolphins or the dock
intro: Hamburg sells ships as well as managing them. Container ship owners and tonnage providers in the city put older Panamax, post-Panamax and feeder tonnage on the market, often as sister ships, and buyers usually see them during a call on the Elbe. A pre-purchase inspection in Hamburg measures what a walk-round cannot: hatch coamings, deck and side structure, ballast tanks, cell guides, reefer power and running machinery. We cover ships at the Burchardkai, Altenwerder and Tollerort terminals, feeders at the mooring dolphins and ships docked on the south bank. The team travels from India for each inspection.

highlights.h: Holds open as the boxes come out
highlights.p: On a container ship working cargo, cellular holds can only be seen once their bays are discharged. We agree the sequence with the chief officer, so tank tops, cell guides and hold bulkheads are examined bay by bay as the gantry cranes empty them.

highlights.h: Sister ships compared like for like
highlights.p: When a Hamburg owner sells several sister ships, a buyer choosing between them gains most from identical inspections. The same spaces, measurement points and machinery readings on each ship make the differences between them plain, instead of hiding them behind differing scopes.

Large ships arrive and leave on the Elbe according to tide and draught, so the time alongside is known in advance but is rarely long. The plan fits the inspection into that slot, and anything the terminal call cannot reach is listed for the buyer.

sections.h: Where can a buyer inspect a ship in Hamburg?
p: Container terminals are where most Hamburg viewings take place, because that is where the ships on the market are working. At Burchardkai, Altenwerder, Tollerort and the Eurogate terminal, work on deck, in the engine room and in the accommodation goes ahead under the ship's own permit system while cargo is handled, and the holds open up as their bays are discharged. Ballast tank entry during cargo work depends on the ballast plan, so the tanks to be prepared are agreed with the master before arrival.

Feeders and short-sea ships lying at the mooring dolphins and lay-by berths between Baltic rotations are reached by launch and give a longer, quieter window. Bulk carriers at the Hansaport ore and coal terminal can be seen in the hours after discharge, tankers at the oil harbour on deck and in the pump room, and multipurpose and heavy-lift ships at the multipurpose berths. A ship docked at Blohm+Voss at Steinwerder or at Norderwerft shows her shell dry, if the seller and the yard both agree to the visit.
list: Burchardkai, Altenwerder, Tollerort and Eurogate: container ships during cargo work, holds bay by bay
Mooring dolphins and lay-by berths: feeders between rotations, with ballast tanks prepared
Hansaport: bulk carrier holds and wing tanks after discharge
Oil harbour tank terminals: tanker deck, piping and pump room under the terminal's rules
Multipurpose and ro-ro berths: tween decks, heavy-lift cranes and ramps
Steinwerder and Norderwerft docks: the shell out of the water, with both the yard and the seller agreeing

sections.h: Which ships do buyers inspect in Hamburg, and why are they for sale?
p: Container ships dominate. Owners in Hamburg manage large fleets of similar ships, and when charters end or a fleet is renewed, older Panamax and post-Panamax tonnage and feeders come onto the market. Their buyers range from liner operators adding capacity to owners who will trade the ships on regional routes. Multipurpose and heavy-lift ships from the city's breakbulk owners, bulk carriers emptied at Hansaport and product and chemical tankers at the oil harbour form the rest of the pre-purchase work.

Age and charter history shape what a buyer needs to know. A container ship that has spent years on charter in demanding ocean trades may have worked its hatch coamings and longitudinal deck structure hard, and a feeder that has served the northern Baltic may have met winter ice, frequent port calls and repeated tug contact. Since emissions trading and FuelEU Maritime began to apply to European voyages, owners and charterers look more closely at the age and condition of the tonnage they take on, so measured evidence now carries more weight in the negotiation.

sections.h: What does a pre-purchase inspection check on a container ship at Hamburg?
p: The structure that carries the hull girder comes first. Hatch coaming top plates and coaming stays are read and examined for cracks, with magnetic particle testing at hatch corners and bracket toes where the master allows a patch to be cleaned; the upper deck strake and sheer strake are measured; and ballast tanks in the double bottom and wing spaces are entered if the crew has prepared them. In the holds, cell guides are checked for bending and detached sections from container impact, tank tops for set-in plating, and bilge wells for wastage.

Hatch covers on a cellular ship are lifted off by the terminal's gantry, so their undersides and seating are best seen when a pontoon has been landed on the quay or on another hatch during cargo work. Lashing bridges, container fittings and the reefer installation follow: a thermal survey of the reefer distribution boards and sockets under load reveals overheating the eye cannot see. In the engine room, generators, pumps and bow thrusters are measured while they run, and the scrubber, where fitted, gets spot thickness readings on its wash-water and overboard piping.

sections.h: What do pre-purchase inspections in Hamburg commonly find?
p: Container ships and the other ships sold from Hamburg tend to show the findings below. Each is reported with its location and photograph, so the buyer can judge it against the class survey status and the last thickness report released through the classification society.
list: Cracks at hatch corners, coaming stays and lashing bridge supports
Wastage on hatch coaming top plates and on the upper deck between hatches
Bent or detached cell guides and set-in tank top plating from container impact
Ballast tank coating breakdown in double-bottom and wing spaces
Overheating at reefer sockets and distribution boards under load
Wall loss in scrubber wash-water and overboard lines
Generators and bow thrusters with vibration that sets them apart from their sister machines

sections.h: How do you plan a pre-purchase inspection around a Hamburg call?
p: Start with the visa and the tide. Each technician travelling from India needs a Schengen visa issued for the job; let us know as soon as the ship's Hamburg call is known, and send the expected arrival and departure, which the Elbe passage fixes for the largest ships. Hamburg Airport lies within the city, so the team reaches the terminals soon after landing, and the seller's agent registers the technicians with the terminal or books the launch for a ship at the dolphins.

Ask the seller, through the broker, for the bay plan and the discharge sequence as well as consent to the spaces on the inspection plan. Knowing which bays empty first lets us place the hold inspection where it fits, and knowing which ballast tanks can be emptied without upsetting the stowage tells the master what to prepare. If the ship is idle between charters, a mooring dolphin or lay-by berth gives a far fuller inspection than a working terminal call. Details can go to info@atlantisndt.com, or use the enquiry form further down.

sections.h: Example scope: comparing sister feeders offered by a Hamburg owner
p: A buyer offered a choice between sister feeders calling at Hamburg on the same Baltic service can have each one inspected on its call, or at the dolphins between rotations, to a single plan. The plan fixes the ballast tanks to be entered, the deck and coaming grid for thickness readings, the hatch corners for crack checks and the machinery to measure, with the same running condition requested on each ship. The report sets the ships side by side: coating ratings, the lowest readings and their locations, crack findings, and the vibration of each generator against its sisters.

Differences that look small on one ship stand out across several: a ballast tank sliding towards POOR on one sister, an extra crack at a hatch corner on another, a generator running rougher than its twins. Records are compared the same way, from class survey status to running hours and the port state control history on Equasis. The buyer then has a reasoned order of preference, while the choice between the ships, and how the negotiation proceeds, remains the buyer's own.

codes: Norwegian Saleform 2012 and SALEFORM 2025 – inspection by the buyers before acceptance
IACS UR Z7 – hull classification surveys, including coating condition terms
MARPOL Annex VI regulation 14 – fuel sulphur in the North Sea ECA and scrubber use
ASTM E797 – pulse-echo contact ultrasonic thickness measurement
ISO 17638 – magnetic particle testing of welds
ISO 20816-1 – evaluation of machine vibration by measurements on non-rotating parts
deliverables: Findings that could affect the buyer's decision, reported before the ship sails
Condition of holds, tanks, deck and hatch covers by space, with photographs placed on the general arrangement
Thickness readings on coamings, deck strakes and ballast tank structure against original values
Crack-check results at hatch corners, coaming stays and lashing bridge supports
Thermal survey of switchboards and reefer distribution, and vibration readings on running machinery
Side-by-side comparison where sister ships are inspected, and a list of items not inspected

faqs.q: Can a container ship be inspected for a buyer during cargo work in Hamburg?
faqs.a: Yes. Deck, engine room and accommodation can be inspected under the ship's permit system while cargo is handled, and the holds become accessible as their bays are discharged. We agree the sequence with the chief officer from the bay plan. Ballast tanks need to be emptied and ventilated in advance, which depends on the stowage, so the master should know before arrival which tanks the buyer wants to see.

faqs.q: How do you fit an inspection into an Elbe call?
faqs.a: The largest ships arrive and leave on the tide, so the time alongside is fixed before the ship reaches the Elbe pilot. We plan the inspection against that slot, ranking the spaces by what matters most to the buyer, and stay in touch with the agent because the arrival can move with tide and traffic. Anything left unseen when she sails is listed in the report for the buyer to weigh.

faqs.q: Can you inspect several sister ships for one buyer at Hamburg?
faqs.a: Yes. Each ship is inspected to the same plan as she calls at Hamburg or lies at the dolphins: the same spaces, the same measurement grid and the same machinery readings in the same running condition. The reports then compare the ships directly, so the buyer can see which one carries the most steel, the best coatings and the healthiest machinery before choosing between them.

faqs.q: Will the class society accept readings from a pre-purchase inspection in Hamburg?
faqs.a: No. A society counts thickness readings towards its surveys only when they come from a firm it has qualified under IACS UR Z17, and the UR Z17 approvals Atlantis is pursuing with DNV, Lloyd's Register and ABS have not yet been issued. Pre-purchase readings are evidence for the buyer, set against the class survey status and thickness reports that the society releases with the seller's consent.

faqs.q: Do you check the reefer installation on a container ship before purchase?
faqs.a: Yes. With reefer containers plugged in and running, a thermal survey of the reefer distribution boards, the sockets and the main switchboard shows loose or overloaded connections as hot spots. Damaged sockets, cables and plugs are noted visually. A ship that discharges her reefers in Hamburg should be surveyed before they come off, so ask the seller for the stowage plan in advance.

faqs.q: Can multipurpose and heavy-lift ships be inspected for buyers at Hamburg?
faqs.a: Yes, at the multipurpose berths or at a lay-by between cargoes. The scope covers holds and tween decks, hatch covers, the heavy-lift cranes and their pedestals, with magnetic particle testing on pedestal welds where a patch can be cleaned, and the ballast and anti-heeling pumps these ships depend on when lifting. Load testing and certification of the cranes stay with their maker or a competent person.
